## 🤖 Claude *(02:47:32)*

<details>
<summary>💭 Thinking Process</summary>

The verification is complete—the assets match perfectly across both versions, with detailed specs confirmed for the master files including duration, resolution, bitrate, and file sizes. The manifest claims 24-bit/48kHz audio with 120s duration, but the actual WAV file is 16-bit PCM at 192kHz mono running 114.632s—a clear discrepancy. I've verified all 13 narration files total exactly 157.1s across 12 unique tracks, and the build configuration locks in 1280×720 resolution at 10s duration with perspective set to 1300, plus absolute pixel positioning confirmed in the render script. The frame count hits 5120 total across all scenes using 634MB, with 14 HTML and 14 JSON scene files plus a 10-line asset manifest, while the script directories contain no media files.

Now I'm confirming the core finding: scanning all 58 videos in scope reveals only two 720×1280 items from GraphoEnterprise as third-party content. The scene-to-content mapping aligns perfectly—each of the 14 scenes maps to specific topics like the gancho intro, Agent Plugins, tool showcases, and the final call-to-action—all corroborated by the JSON metadata and frame data.

The arithmetic checks out: 165.44 seconds across 14 clips with 11 pieces ranging 11-21 seconds, roughly 5 cuts at 30 seconds each, fitting within an 11-12 day production ceiling. But I'm finding three corrections to the asset inventory: the scene PNG count is actually 13, not 14 as claimed, with the directory containing 15 PNGs total (13 scene images plus contact sheet and regeneration preview) along with video files totaling 17 items. The resolution field was left blank, but those 13 scene PNGs are actually 1024×1024 square format.

The bigger issue is the aspect ratio mismatch—those square images don't account for the 9:16 vertical format needed for Stories and Reels, which would require padding or extension. And the ep06-master-v32 card layout claim about centered typography with vertical breathing room is materially wrong: the title is actually left-aligned at 72 pixels from the edge, and when cropped to 9:16 (608×1080 from x=656), the header gets cut off entirely, both neon cards clip, and the caption truncates. The vertical empty space doesn't matter for a 16:9 to 9:16 conversion—the real constraint is horizontal extent that needs removal.

I'm also catching some descriptive inaccuracies in the source material: veo-p1 is labeled as a medium frontal shot but the frame at t=3 is actually a tight head-and-shoulders close-up, which actually supports the crop-survivability argument. The c07 scene description calls it a "Muse benchmark" when it's really showing an index score (02 · O NÚMERO / AA Intelligence Index / 51 → 54). And the symphony track timing doesn't add up—the movements are listed as 30.2 + 45.3 + 45.3 seconds, which totals 120.744 seconds, but the continuous master is 114.672 seconds.

There's also a separate finding outside the scope: 26 additional videos exist in the canvas-design/open-design/ folder (21 at 1920x1080, 5 at 1280x720), all third-party template previews. None are vertical, so they don't affect the inventory, and they're outside the declared scope anyway.

For the final count: 38 total items in the inventory, all verified to some degree. Three refutations were found, but they only hit two distinct items—the assets/ item and the ep06-master-v32 item—so that's 2 items refuted or corrected, leaving 36 confirmed. Continuing through the rest of the items—GraphoEnterprise files, WhatsApp versions, audio tracks, video files, and various directories for scenes, frames, and assets. That brings the total to 39 items, though I'm noting that the assets directory itself might be redundant since there are already asset files listed separately.

Looking at the refutations more carefully: the first error was an arithmetic discrepancy with the PNG count, and the second involves a claim about reframe-friendliness that doesn't hold up. That leaves 37 items confirmed out of 39. The core measurements—durations, resolutions, file counts—all check out precisely. The issues are really in the descriptive language and interpretive claims rather than the actual data. Given the available categories, this feels like PARCIAL, though the measurement accuracy is genuinely solid.…

## 🤖 Claude *(02:48:38)*

<details>
<summary>💭 Thinking Process</summary>

I found the actual EP06 generator script—it's built with proportional sizing from the ground up, not fixed pixels. The dimensions scale based on aspect ratio, and every position and size is calculated as a fraction of the canvas width and height, then converted to pixels.

The portrait mode (9:16) has its own dedicated type scale across seven text elements with specific size ratios, plus a hero-scale reduction factor. This isn't leftover code—it's a deliberate, fully-implemented portrait path.

The inventory's "capacidade" entry is wrong on multiple fronts: it points to the wrong generator file entirely (the motion spike builder, not the actual EP06 template), and its claim about absolute positioning breaking on aspect ratio inversion misquotes the actual layout structure.

The real EP06 template uses purely proportional sizing (`Math.round(W*k)` and `Math.round(H*k)`), so flipping to 9:16 is genuinely just one field change in the scene spec plus swapping the dimensions passed to the renderer—far simpler than the inventory suggested. I haven't actually run a 9:16 render myself, but the infrastructure is provably there and functional.…

</details>
